pages.title: About
pages.body:
Northline Athletics started in 2019 with one question: why does good training kit either feel great or last, but rarely both? We design in small batches, test every piece on real miles and real reps, and only release something when we would wear it ourselves.

How we work

Every fabric is tested for stretch recovery, opacity and wash durability. We use recycled polyester wherever it performs as well as the alternative, and we publish where each piece is made.

Who it is for

Early-morning runners, lunchtime lifters, weekend trail people and everyone in between.

pages.title: Contact
pages.body:
Questions about sizing, an order or a product? Send us a message and a real person will reply within one business day.

Customer care is open Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm Pacific.

pages.title: Frequently asked questions
pages.body:
How do your sizes fit?

Tops and bottoms are true to size with an athletic cut. Each product page lists model height and the size worn. If you are between sizes, size up for a relaxed fit.

How should I wash my gear?

Machine wash cold with like colors, skip fabric softener and hang to dry. This keeps the stretch and the finish working for longer.

Can I change or cancel an order?

We can change an order within one hour of purchase. Contact us as soon as you can and we will do our best.

Do you restock sold-out items?

Most core styles return within six weeks. Use the notify option on the product page, or contact us.

pages.title: Shipping
pages.body:
Delivery times

Standard shipping takes three to five business days in the United States. Express shipping takes one to two business days. Orders placed before 1 pm Pacific usually leave the warehouse the same day.

Shipping costs

Standard shipping is free on orders over $75. Below that, it is a flat $6. Express shipping is $15.

International

We ship to Canada and the United Kingdom. Duties and taxes are shown at checkout.

pages.title: Returns
pages.body:
30-day returns

If something is not right, return it within 30 days of delivery. Items must be unworn, unwashed and have their tags attached.

How to return

Contact us with your order number and we will email a prepaid label for orders in the United States. Refunds go to the original payment method within five business days of us receiving the parcel.

Exchanges

Need a different size? Place a new order and return the original item, which gets you the new size sooner.

articles.title: Build a base before your first 10K
articles.author: Maya Okafor
articles.summary: Six weeks of easy running will do more for your first 10K than any speed session.
articles.body:
Most new runners start too fast. The first month is about teaching your legs and tendons to handle repeated impact, not about pace.

Start with time, not distance

Run for 20 to 30 minutes at a pace where you can speak in full sentences. Do it three times a week and add five minutes to one run every week.

Add strides in week four

After an easy run, add four 20-second relaxed pickups with full recovery. They wake up your running form without adding much stress.

By week six most people can run 40 minutes continuously, which is the base a 10K plan needs.

articles.title: The case for the easy run
articles.author: Daniel Reyes
articles.summary: Why the slowest run of your week might be the one that makes you faster.
articles.body:
Easy runs build your aerobic engine and let hard days stay hard. If every run is medium effort, you are too tired to run fast and too fast to recover.

A good test: if you cannot chat comfortably, slow down. Your heart rate will thank you, and your pace will improve over the next few months.

Keep two-thirds of your weekly running at this effort and protect your quality days.

articles.title: How to pack a gym bag so you actually go
articles.author: Maya Okafor
articles.summary: A short checklist that removes the excuses before they start.
articles.body:
The best gym bag is the one that is already packed. Keep a second set of essentials in the bag so you never have to hunt for them.

  • Spare socks and a clean base layer
  • A lightweight towel
  • Insulated bottle, filled the night before
  • Headphones and a charging cable
  • A zip pouch for your keys and wallet

Put shoes in the ventilated compartment and wet kit in the wet pocket, and your bag will smell fine for years.

articles.title: What to wear for cold-weather running
articles.author: Daniel Reyes
articles.summary: Dress for how you will feel ten minutes in, not when you step outside.
articles.body:
A common rule is to dress as if it were 10 degrees Celsius warmer than the thermometer says. You should feel slightly cool when you start.

Layer smart

A light base layer, a vest for your core and thin gloves cover most conditions down to freezing. Add tights below about 5 degrees Celsius.

Be seen

Winter means dark mornings. Reflective details and a light make you easier to spot.

articles.title: Strength training for runners: two sessions, 30 minutes
articles.author: Priya Nair
articles.summary: Two short sessions a week can reduce injury risk and improve your running economy.
articles.body:
You do not need a long gym routine. Two 30-minute sessions a week cover what matters most for runners.

The essentials

Split squats, hip hinges, calf raises, step-ups and a few core exercises like planks and side planks. Do three sets of eight to ten reps with a challenging load.

Schedule them after an easy run or on a rest day, never before a key workout.

articles.title: A simple recovery routine for busy weeks
articles.author: Priya Nair
articles.summary: Ten minutes after training can make tomorrow's session feel better.
articles.body:
Recovery does not need gadgets. A few habits make the biggest difference.

  • Walk for five minutes after hard efforts to bring your heart rate down
  • Drink water and eat protein within an hour
  • Spend five minutes on gentle mobility for hips and calves
  • Go to bed at the same time each night

Consistency beats intensity, especially when the week is full.
